claims.text: The initial Ti–Ni-based high-entropy alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution with titanium and nickel as primary constituents.
Aging at approximately 900°C for 1 hour under approximately 0.3 atm partial nitrogen pressure, followed by slow cooling, is the proposed intervention.
The proposed nitrogen aging treatment will form Ti2N precipitates in situ.
The Ti2N precipitates produced by the treatment will be nanoscale, fine, and coherent with the matrix.
Slow cooling after nitrogen aging will promote nanoscale coherent Ti2N precipitation.
The Ti2N precipitates will be uniformly dispersed throughout the parent matrix.
Ti2N precipitates will impede dislocation motion during high-temperature deformation.
Ti2N precipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature deformation.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will enhance elevated-temperature yield strength.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will improve creep resistance.
The nitrogen-aged alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than an inert-aged control.
The nitrogen-aged alloy will have a lower creep rate than the control.
The nitrogen-aged alloy will have improved creep rupture life and overall elevated-temperature mechanical performance relative to the control.
The proposed performance benefit applies at test temperatures up to approximately 700°C.
The proposed performance benefit is limited to inert or controlled atmospheres that prevent significant surface oxidation.
The proposed intervention is applicable only when the alloy maintains a single-phase structure after treatment.
Ti2N precipitates may coarsen during processing or high-temperature testing.
Poorly controlled processing may produce embrittlement or deleterious coarse precipitates.

contradictions.description: The boundary requires the alloy to remain single-phase after treatment, while the hypothesis and structural mediator require formation of Ti2N precipitates, which constitute a distinct precipitate phase and therefore make the treated microstructure multiphase.
